data.exact_reserve_text: Included within net claims incurred is adverse prior year development relating to certain financial lines classes; reduced by positive developments across a number of other classes. Additionally, prior accident year reserves have been strengthened for inflation loadings.

prior_year_events.event_name: Adverse prior development on Financial Lines
prior_year_events.impact_description: Adverse prior year development relating to certain financial lines classes resulting in strengthening of prior year reserves.

Some late notifications for Covid related claims; reporting delays led to strengthening on UK Liability business but fears of long-term illness and long Covid did not materialise in claims numbers or indemnity paid.

named_events.loss_description: Some late notifications for Covid related claims; fears of long-term illness and long Covid have not materialised through claims numbers and indemnity paid.

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2022 were GBP 1,269.6m. During 2022 there was adverse prior year development on prior accident years amounting to a gross strengthening of GBP 39.8m (approximately 3.1% of opening gross reserves). The movement was driven primarily by adverse prior year development in financial lines and inflation-related strengthening of prior accident year reserves, partially offset by favourable developments in other classes.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from balance sheet comparative column (Claims outstanding 2021: 1,269.6). Prior year development (gross) sourced from Technical Provisions note: 'Claims expense - previous financial year 39.8' (gross). The report gives narrative references to adverse development in Financial Lines and inflation-strengthening but does not quantify prior-year movements by line of business; lob_movements are therefore directional and inferred. A gross claims development triangle is present and has been captured; no RITC distortion noted in the main technical provisions for the annual accounts, but the underwriting year accounts show RITC activity for the 2020 closed year which could distort YOA-specific analyses if not considered.
